# glb-animation-handoff

Purpose: Document GLB animation contract (skeletal vs morph, FPS, looping, root motion, blend transitions) with truthful caveats for web playback.

When a GLB ships with animation, capture the exact playback contract the consumer needs (which clips exist, how to start them, what loops, what does not) so the web side does not guess.

Metadata: Contract `v1.0.0` | Category `evidence-and-handoff` | Role `rig-and-animation-clip-handoff-planner` | Tier `L0` | Runtime default `Not Run` | Artifact default `Not Produced` | Mutation `downgrade_only`

## When to use & trigger cues
- the GLB has at least one animation clip
- before final glb-web-handoff
- when the consumer is a web app (Three.js / R3F / Babylon / model-viewer)
- when the user mentions "idle", "loop", "transition", "interactive trigger"
- Trigger phrases: "make it loop", "trigger animation on hover", "idle and active states", "smooth transition between"

## When not to use (delegation boundaries)
- static GLBs with no animation → use `glb-web-handoff` (`references/skill-glb-web-handoff.md`; Delegates out-of-scope requests to glb-web-handoff)
- video pre-renders → use `output-format-decision` (`references/skill-output-format-decision.md`; Delegates out-of-scope requests to output-format-decision)
- platforms that re-author animation downstream (game engines re-rigging the asset) → use `product-hero-scene-planner` (`references/skill-product-hero-scene-planner.md`; game engines re-rigging the asset)

## Input & output contract
- Required input `animation_clip_inventory` (`array`): List of NLA/action clips with frame lengths, FPS, and skeletal/morph types
- Required input `interactive_playback_triggers` (`object`): Target loop/one-shot semantics, crossfade durations, root-motion policy, and consumer triggers
- Optional input `mobile_rig_budget_ceilings` (`object`): Bone count, morph target, and keyframe channel ceilings from glb-mobile-performance-budget
- Output contract: `per_clip_animation_contract_table`, `root_motion_and_interpolation_pins`, `consumer_playback_verification_checklist` (Runtime status: `Not Run`, Artifact status: `Not Produced`, `downgrade_only`).

## Quick-start steps
1. enumerate every animation clip in the scene plan or exported GLB
2. mark the type of each clip (skeletal / morph / both)
3. pin FPS, loop semantics, transitions, root-motion treatment
4. flag web-playback caveats per clip (Three.js animationMixer, glTF spec quirks)

## Safety boundaries & non-goals
- Runtime boundary: This skill is documentation-only. It never exports GLB, runs Blender, writes Python, or claims that a clip plays correctly without measured evidence (`render-export-evidence` for export proof plus manual viewer test for playback).
- Run Blender or export GLB files.
- Author, retarget, or modify animations.
- Generate Python or `bpy` snippets.
- Promise web-side playback smoothness or upgrade truth states.
